newsitem.title: USA: Police continue probe in murder of Colorado child.
newsitem.headline: Police continue probe in murder of Colorado child.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey on Tuesday offered little new information on the case, saying they still hope to set up a formal interview with the girl's parents.

"The Ramseys are not under arrest," Leslie Aaholm, Boulder police spokeswoman said. "Police have been working on setting up an interview, a formal interview (with the parents) and they will continue to try that," she told a news briefing.

John and Patricia Ramsey, in an interview with CNN, denied any involvement in their daughter's murder. But both have hired attorneys and have yet to be interviewed formally by Boulder police. He is a prominent executive and she is a former Miss West Virginia.

Boulder Police Chief Tom Koby has kept a lid on information in the case and has even reassigned one of the five Boulder detectives sent to Georgia, citing a need for the police to remain focused on finding the killer and not being distracted by media attention.
Police spokesman Kelvin McNeill declined to comment further on the matter, saying it was a personnel issue.
A state court judge in Boulder on Tuesday refused a media request to unseal affidavits in the case.

The little girl's body was found on Dec. 26 in the basement of the family's 15-room home about eight hours after her mother said she had found a ransom note demanding $118,000 on the back staircase of the Boulder residence.
